summary: Lungtok Tenpai Nyima (1927–2017) worked in Tibetology and religious studies. He earned a Geshe degree at Kyangtsang Monastery and studied under Horwa Drungrampa Tendzin Lodro Gyatso. He founded Menri Monastery, serving as its abbot from 1969.

Luo Changpei (1899–1958) was a scholar in linguistics and Sinology. After studying at Peking University (~1916–1921), he held posts at Northwest University (~1924–1926), Xiamen University (~1926–1927), Sun Yat-sen University (~1928–1929), and Peking University (~1934–1950).

Lutz Bieg (born 1943) is a Sinologist who earned his Dr. phil. at Heidelberg University (~1965–1971) and his Habilitation at Freie Universität Berlin (by 1986). From 1989 to 2008, he was a full professor at the University of Cologne.

Lynn Thomas works in Indology and religious studies. Thomas earned a BA and MA at Lancaster University and completed a D.Phil at the University of Oxford in 1987, later serving as a lecturer in Hinduism at the University of Roehampton (attested 1997).

Léon Feer (1830–1902) was a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied under Philippe-Édouard Foucaux and Étienne Marc Quatremère, later holding posts at INALCO (Chair of Tibetan, 1864), the Collège de France (1869–1872), and the Bibliothèque nationale (1872).

Léon Vandermeersch (1928–2021) was a Sinologist and philosopher. He studied at INALCO, the University of Paris, EPHE, and Paris Diderot University. His posts included Aix-Marseille University, Paris Diderot, EPHE (director of studies, 1979–1993), and EFEO (director, 1989–1993).

Lê Mạnh Thát (born 1944) works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and history and archaeology. He earned a BA from Saigon University (~1962–1965) and a PhD from the University of Wisconsin–Madison (~1965–1974), later holding a post at Van Hanh University (~1974–1975).
M. Athar Ali (1925–1998) was an Indologist and historian. He studied at Aligarh Muslim University from ~1948 to 1961 and served as a historian on the faculty there from ~1953 to 1995.
M. D. Balasubrahmanyam specialized in Indology and linguistics. He completed his dissertation and later held an academic post at Savitribai Phule Pune University (attested 1967).

M. G. Dhadphale (born 1937) is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He served as a professor at Tilak Maharashtra Vidyapeeth (attested 2000) and as editor of the Annals at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (attested 2003).

M. H. Krishna (1892–1947) was a historian and Indologist. Educated at Maharaja's College, Mysore, University of Madras, and UCL under Ernest Arthur Gardner, he served as Professor of History, department head, and dean of arts at the University of Mysore.

M. R. Raghava Varier (born 1936) is an Indologist, historian, and linguist. Educated at the University of Calicut, the Archaeological Survey of India, and Jawaharlal Nehru University, he served as a professor at the University of Calicut from ~1978 to 2000.

M. S. A. Rao (1926–1985) was an Indologist who studied at the University of Delhi and the University of Mumbai under Govind Sadashiv Ghurye. He held positions at the University of Delhi (~1955–1985), Syracuse University, and the University of Pennsylvania.

M. S. Nagaraja Rao (1932–2011) was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at the University of Mysore, Savitribai Phule Pune University, and under M. N. Deshpande. He held posts at Karnatak University, Karnataka State Archaeology Department, and the ASI.

M. Seshagiri Sastri worked in Indology and linguistics. In 1899, he was attested as Professor of Sanskrit and Comparative Philology at Presidency University and as Curator at the Government Oriental Manuscripts Library.

M. Shinoda (born 1977) is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. Shinoda's education includes studies at Agoura High School, Art Center College of Design, and study under teacher Seiren Matsunami.

M. Yamunacharya was a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied under Mysore Hiriyanna, Ardeshir Ruttonji Wadia, and Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan. He served as Professor in Philosophy at Maharaja's College, Mysore.

M.L. Pattaratorn Chirapravati (born 1958) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and art history. Educated at Silpakorn, Ohio State, and Cornell universities, she served as Associate Professor at California State University, Sacramento (2002–2016), among other museum and academic posts.

Maanasa Visweswaran works in Indology and computational studies. In 2026, Visweswaran is attested as a student and project staff member (Wissenschaftliche Projektmitarbeiterin) at the University of Hamburg.

Mabel Bode (1864–1922) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Bern and studied under T. W. Rhys Davids and Sylvain Lévi. She taught at University College London (1909–1917) and SOAS.
